description: Semantic review of individual units in pdf_corpus_coverage.json. Each entry is bound to the page-text digest it was reviewed against; build_pdf_ledger.py refuses to apply an entry whose unit or digest has changed.

entries.title: Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

exact_difference.detail: the unit requires an allowlist for caller-supplied fetch targets and forbids returning the upstream response; the rule adds resolved-address authorization, per-redirect re-authorization, and the DNS-rebinding window

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule's address policy is stated for IPv4 and IPv6 ranges the unit does not enumerate; deployments behind egress proxies may need a different enforcement point

entries.title: Arbitrary file read

exact_difference.detail: the unit shows a read path built by concatenating a caller-supplied id onto a root, exploited with ..; the rule states the containment contract that rejects it

entries.remaining_uncertainty: symlink traversal inside the root is stated as a contract item but is platform-dependent to enforce

entries.title: Arbitrary file write

exact_difference.detail: the unit shows the write-side of the same defect, where an uploaded file name escapes the upload directory; the rule covers read, write, and delete alike

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none beyond the read-side entry

entries.title: Denial of Service (DoS)

exact_difference.detail: the unit describes denial of service through resource exhaustion and notes that blocking the async event loop lets a small number of requests stall a service; the rule adds explicit byte, deadline, and concurrency ceilings

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule does not prescribe values; limits are per-route capacity decisions

entries.title: Authenticated encryption (AEAD)

exact_difference.detail: the unit introduces authenticated encryption as the construction that removes block-cipher and MAC composition footguns; the rule requires an AEAD

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Common problems and pitfalls with cryptography

exact_difference.detail: the unit states that key management is hard, that AEAD should be preferred, that primitives should not be implemented locally, and that side channels and non-constant-time code defeat correctness testing; the rule states the same contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: constant-time behaviour cannot be proven by a portable test; the assertion covers the comparison contract, not the generated code

entries.title: The Rust cryptography ecosystem

exact_difference.detail: the unit is a 2021 survey of Rust cryptography crates; crate-by-crate recommendations age out and are not a durable coding contract for this library

entries.remaining_uncertainty: if a future rule names specific crates, it must be re-derived from current advisories rather than this survey

entries.title: Vendoring dependencies

exact_difference.detail: the unit gives the reasons to vendor dependencies (offline builds, privacy, reviewable update diffs) and the repository-size cost, with a private registry as the alternative; the rule states the same trade-off

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Automated audits

exact_difference.detail: the unit covers automated auditing of a dependency tree, including advisory scanning; the rules place that in the CI gate and in the admission policy

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Writing and Running Integration Tests

exact_difference.detail: the unit establishes POSIX exit status (0 success, non-zero failure) and black-box testing of the built binary; the rules add stream routing, broken-pipe handling, and the stdin conventions

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rules describe the pattern with std process APIs; the unit uses assert_cmd, which is named in the rule text but not depended on

entries.title: How cat Works

exact_difference.detail: the unit documents the convention that a file argument of - means standard input, and that absent arguments read stdin; the rule states it as contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Notes from the Testing Underground

exact_difference.detail: the unit collects the book's testing practices, including golden output and the note that listings carry owners and modification times which differ per machine; test-cli-blackbox states the process-level assertions and test-env-independent the normalization contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: one entry carries two rules: the assertion named here covers the CLI stream contract, and golden_output_asserts_program_fields_and_normalizes_host_fields covers normalization

entries.title: Borrowing and Lifetimes

exact_difference.detail: the unit derives variance from subtyping, shows that &mut T is invariant in T, and shows the two-lifetime remedy for a struct holding &'a mut &'b str; the rule states that contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the PhantomData guidance in the rule is stated more briefly than the unit's later treatment of pointer types

entries.title: Conditional Compilation

exact_difference.detail: the unit recommends auditing dependencies with cargo-deny and cargo-audit for advisories, duplicate major versions, unmaintained crates, and license policy; the rule states the same admission and audit policy

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Versioning

exact_difference.detail: the unit covers Cargo semantic versioning, the MSRV minor-bump technique, minimal dependency versions, changelogs, and prerelease versioning between releases; the rule states each as contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: minimal-version resolution remains an unstable Cargo flag, so the rule's verification step depends on nightly

entries.title: Additional Testing Tools

exact_difference.detail: the unit covers fuzzing, property testing, Miri, Loom, and benchmark variance; the mapped rules state each, with fuzzing and sanitizers newly added

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the unit is an early-access edition; tool names were re-checked against current releases before the rules were written

entries.title: Coping with Fear

exact_difference.detail: the unit requires running unsafe code through Miri and sanitizers in CI, notes that both only observe executed paths, and asks for assertions in unsafe code; the rules state the same

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Sane Concurrency

exact_difference.detail: the unit covers ThreadSanitizer for larger concurrent tests, its constant-factor overhead, and its nightly -Zsanitizer=thread requirement; the rule states it

entries.remaining_uncertainty: sanitizer availability is target-specific, which the rule notes but cannot enumerate

entries.title: Protect Your Secrets - secrecy

exact_difference.detail: the unit introduces a secret wrapper because instrumentation captures arguments by default, and identifies the masked Debug implementation as the key property, with wiping as a nice-to-have; the rule states that contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule shows a local wrapper so the example compiles without the crate; production use should take the maintained crate

entries.title: 9.2 Sources of time

exact_difference.detail: the unit distinguishes the sources of time available to a process, including the real-time clock and the operating system's system clock

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 9.3 Definitions

exact_difference.detail: the unit defines absolute time, the system clock and its jumps, monotonicity, and steady clocks with equal-length seconds suited to measuring durations; the rule states which clock each use requires

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 9.7 clock v0.1.2: Setting the time

exact_difference.detail: the unit warns that setting the system clock makes it jump and can destabilize applications that expect monotonically increasing time; the rule turns that into a type-level split between measurement and timestamps

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 9.9 clock v0.1.3: Resolving differences between clocks with the Network Time Protocol (NTP)

exact_difference.detail: the unit builds an NTP client that adjusts the local clock toward server time, which is the mechanism that makes wall-clock differences unreliable for measurement

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Reading Bytes from a File

exact_difference.detail: the unit reads a fixed number of bytes from a file and converts them lossily when they may not be valid UTF-8; err-short-read states the contract for the returned count, and type-text-decode-policy makes the strict-versus-lossy choice explicit and requires the substitution to be visible to the caller

entries.remaining_uncertainty: one entry carries two rules: the assertion named here covers the short-read half, and strict_and_lossy_decoding_are_distinguishable_choices covers the decode half

entries.title: 7.7.2 Processing an individual record

exact_difference.detail: the unit processes an individual stored record and checks its integrity before use; the rule generalizes that into which profile a check must survive, naming debug_assert as unusable for boundary data

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the unit does not itself discuss debug versus release assertions; the rule states the contract the unit's code depends on

entries.title: Constrained

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Constrained", pp.54-59) covers auto traits (Send, Sync, Unpin, UnwindSafe, and leakage through impl Trait) as hidden promises of any public type, and recommends pinning them with a compile-only generic function; err-send-sync-static already covered the error-type specialization of this (errors must be Send + Sync + 'static for downcast), and api-auto-trait-contract generalizes it to any public type with a working compile-only assertion and the semver consequence of a private-field regression

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's compile-only assertion example (fn is_normal<T: Sized + Send + Sync + Unpin>()) is restated with different bound choices; the assertion in this ledger proves the happy-path case compiles, not that a regression is caught, which would need a compile-fail harness

entries.title: 5.2.1 Understanding endianness

exact_difference.detail: the unit explains endianness and the difference between host and declared byte order for values that leave the process; the rule states the boundary conversion contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 7.2.1 Writing data to disk with serde and the bincode format

exact_difference.detail: the unit writes structured data to disk with a positional encoding; the rule adds the magic identifier, version marker, and unknown-version rejection that make such a format safe to evolve

entries.remaining_uncertainty: migration strategy between versions is stated as a contract item rather than demonstrated

entries.title: 7.7.4 Validating I/O errors with checksums

exact_difference.detail: the unit validates stored records with a checksum before trusting them; the rule states that contract including the protected span and the mismatch policy

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule distinguishes checksums from keyed MACs, which the unit does not

entries.title: Building the application

exact_difference.detail: the unit returns errors as responses from a web application; the rule adds the requirement that framework-generated failures share the same media type and schema

entries.remaining_uncertainty: no runtime assertion: the contract is about representation across framework-generated paths, which test-http-blackbox covers at the router level

entries.title: Injections

exact_difference.detail: the unit states the general root cause of injection — mishandled program input reaching an interpreter — and enumerates input sources; it does not cover OS command injection specifically, so the rule's subprocess contract (argument vector, no shell, option-terminator, bounded child) extends it

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the corpus contains no unit dedicated to command injection; the rule's specifics are derived from the general principle rather than from a worked example

entries.title: Adding sessions

exact_difference.detail: the unit stores a session — auth, token, headers and cookies — in a file whose path is derived from the host it belongs to; proj-secret-file-mode adds the permission contract for creating that file, and api-credential-scope states the binding as scheme, host and port, re-checked at attach time and dropped across redirects

entries.remaining_uncertainty: one entry carries two rules: the assertion named here covers the file mode, and a_credential_is_withheld_from_every_other_origin covers the origin binding

entries.title: Finding the Files

exact_difference.detail: the unit walks and names files where paths are not guaranteed to be valid Unicode; the rule states the carry-as-Path contract with display-only conversion

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 12.6 Handling signals with custom actions

exact_difference.detail: the unit states that signal handlers have reduced scope, must avoid code that can itself raise signals, and should do nothing but set a flag the application polls; the rule keeps that contract and replaces the unit's `static mut` with an atomic static, since accessing a mutable static is unsafe and racy with a second handler

entries.remaining_uncertainty: signal registration is platform-specific and is described rather than asserted; the test covers the flag contract only

entries.title: Solution

exact_difference.detail: the unit walks directories and handles each entry's Result individually, printing failures to stderr and continuing; the rule adds the ordering, symlink, and bounding requirements

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the unit uses a walker crate; the rule states the contract with std so it holds for either

entries.title: Processing the Files

exact_difference.detail: the unit lifts a compiled pattern out of the per-line loop into a lazily initialized static; the rule states that as a contract with the buffer and immutability caveats

entries.remaining_uncertainty: no runtime assertion: the property is a cost, not an observable behavior, and perf-profile-first governs how to confirm it

entries.title: 9.8 Improving error handling

exact_difference.detail: the unit checks the status returned by a system call and converts failure through the OS error state into a Rust error; the rule states that boundary contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule's handle-ownership and out-parameter points are stated but not asserted

entries.title: XSS

exact_difference.detail: the unit shows a stored cross-site scripting payload delivered as an uploaded SVG that an application accepts and serves back to its users; the rule states the serving contract that neutralizes it — server-chosen type, forced download, nosniff, separate origin

entries.remaining_uncertainty: origin separation and CSP are stated as contract items; the assertion covers the header decision only

entries.title: Traits and Trait Bounds

exact_difference.detail: the unit describes monomorphization's cost in compile time, binary size and instruction cache, and gives the non-generic inner function pattern with the warning not to place the helper in a generic impl block; the rule states that contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the size win is not asserted: it is a code-size property, and perf-profile-first governs measuring it

entries.title: Declarative Macros

exact_difference.detail: the unit states that macro hygiene does not cover types, that exported macros must use fully specified paths such as ::core::option::Option and ::alloc::boxed::Box, that $crate names the defining crate, and that ::std should be avoided so macros work in no_std crates

entries.remaining_uncertainty: no runtime assertion: the property is name resolution, demonstrated by the rule's example compiling under shadowed Result and Option

entries.title: 7.7.1 Initializing the ActionKV struct

exact_difference.detail: the unit's load loop breaks on UnexpectedEof while returning every other error, and its sidebar explains that EOF is a convention rather than a marker in the file; the rule turns that into a contract separating a torn tail from interior corruption, with the recovered length and idempotent replay

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the unit's format carries a per-record checksum, which api-record-checksum covers; this rule assumes that check exists

entries.title: 8.4.2 Converting a hostname to an IP address

exact_difference.detail: the unit resolves a hostname over UDP with a DNS client that generates a random, never-zero message identifier per query; the rule states the defensive contract — verify the source address and match the reply identifier before parsing — and notes that neither check is authentication

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the unit does not discuss forged replies directly; the threat model is supplied by the rule

entries.title: Defining and Validating the Arguments

exact_difference.detail: the unit reads the current date once and passes it to the code that formats and highlights it, rather than re-reading the clock per use; the rule states that as a contract

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: 11.2.3 Source code listings

exact_difference.detail: the unit writes to a memory-mapped framebuffer through write_volatile inside an unsafe block; the rule states why volatile is required and what it does not provide

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the rule's access-width and ownership points extend beyond the unit's single example

entries.title: Defining the Arguments

exact_difference.detail: the unit builds its matcher with a case-insensitivity setting driven by a flag instead of folding the input; the rule states that contract and the Unicode caveat

entries.remaining_uncertainty: none

entries.title: Working with complex types

exact_difference.detail: the unit constructs a host-side typed array over the module's linear memory and frees what it allocated in a finally block, and its surrounding pages hand-marshal a String across the boundary by having the host read raw pointer/length words out of the struct's private layout; ffi-wasm-memory-view adds that any call which can grow memory invalidates that view, and ffi-wasm-wire-abi adds that the (ptr, len) pair must be an explicit, documented wire contract rather than a read of #[repr(Rust)]'s undocumented layout

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the wire-ABI assertion runs on a 64-bit host, not a real wasm32 target, so ptr/len are u64 there instead of the u32 a real WASM export would use; the marshalling shape is the same

entries.title: 7.5 Implementing a key-value store with a log-structured, append-only storage architecture

exact_difference.detail: the unit claims the append-only architecture guarantees data is never lost and stored files are never corrupted, but states no syscall-level contract for reaching that guarantee; the rule supplies the whole-file half of it — same-directory temporary, sync_all before the rename, rename rather than truncate, directory sync afterwards — and states the Windows difference the unit does not mention

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the assertion proves the failure-partway case with an injected write error; it cannot prove the ordering that sync_all and the directory sync buy, which only a power loss or a filesystem fault injector would show

entries.title: Watering holes

exact_difference.detail: the unit covers watering-hole and bitsquatting attacks, including generating ASCII near-miss domains and registering visually similar hostnames to lure victims to a phishing page; it does not name the Unicode-homoglyph/IDNA variant of the same attack or state a canonicalize-before-trust defense, so the rule extends it to that adjacent identity-spoofing class and gives the Rust-side construction discipline

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source page discusses ASCII bitsquatting specifically; the rule's homoglyph/Punycode framing is drawn from general IDN-homograph knowledge rather than from this page, which is recorded as an extension rather than a restatement

entries.title: More advanced techniques for your RAT

exact_difference.detail: the unit's advanced-techniques section covers signing auto-update payloads with a private key so an unsigned channel cannot be used for remote takeover of every agent; the rule states the full verify-before-install contract the source only sketches: embedding the verification key at build time (not fetching it from the update channel), verifying the exact installed bytes rather than a pointer to them, rejecting version replay/rollback, and failing closed when verification itself cannot run

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source states the goal (sign updates) in a few sentences without a worked Rust example; the rollback-replay requirement and the build-time key-embedding discipline are this rule's own additions, not restatements of source text

entries.title: Great Power

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Great Power", pp.148-151) states that offset/add/sub are UB if the result leaves the original allocation "even if you never dereference" it; the rule restates this as a falsifiable contract with a bounded-walk example and a Miri-verification requirement the source states only in prose

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source states the provenance rule in a few sentences without a worked bounds-respecting traversal; the loop-with-a-one-past-the-end-sentinel construction is this rule's own addition

entries.title: Great Responsibility

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Great Responsibility", pp.157-166) covers drop-check and the #[may_dangle]+PhantomData interaction, including the nightly-only escape hatch; the rule states the stable-Rust half only — a raw-pointer-holding wrapper needs PhantomData<T> for drop-check to see it as owning a T at all — since #[may_dangle] cannot appear in a stable-toolchain compiled example

entries.remaining_uncertainty: #[may_dangle] itself (feature dropck_eyepatch) is nightly-only and is mentioned in this rule's prose only, not compiled; the assertion proves the ordinary PhantomData<T> case runs a value's destructor exactly once, not the lifetime-rejection half of dropck, which would need a compile-fail harness

entries.title: Types Across Language Boundaries

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Types Across Language Boundaries", pp.204-211) covers C enumerations that are bitsets (a repr(C) fieldless enum's only valid values are its listed discriminants), allocator identity for pointers crossing FFI, caller- vs callee-owned buffers, tying a foreign object's lifetime to a Rust borrow, and typed opaque pointers instead of void*; the two rules split this into the enum/bitflag half and the resource-ownership/typed-handle half, each with its own worked example the source states only in prose

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's tagged-union layout guidance for data-carrying repr(C) enums is not covered by either rule and remains a documented gap

entries.title: Constrained

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Constrained", pp.54-59) covers auto traits (Send, Sync, Unpin, UnwindSafe, and leakage through impl Trait) as hidden promises of any public type, and recommends pinning them with a compile-only generic function; err-send-sync-static already covered the error-type specialization of this (errors must be Send + Sync + 'static for downcast), and api-auto-trait-contract generalizes it to any public type with a working compile-only assertion and the semver consequence of a private-field regression

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's compile-only assertion example (fn is_normal<T: Sized + Send + Sync + Unpin>()) is restated with different bound choices; the assertion in this ledger proves the happy-path case compiles, not that a regression is caught, which would need a compile-fail harness

entries.title: 1.9.1 Heartbleed

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("1.9.1 Heartbleed", p.47) names the case study by name but does not state the general contract; the rule states it as a falsifiable pattern (disclose the written count, not the buffer's length or capacity) with a reused-buffer example showing a shorter response never carries a longer prior response's leftover tail

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source page is a two-paragraph case-study summary; the rule's reused-buffer construction and its assertion are this rule's own addition, not restated from the source

entries.title: 8.4.1 What is a port number?

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("8.4.1 What is a port number?", starting p.287) sits at the point in the chapter where the source states that a one-shot HTTP/1.1 client must force Connection: close and that TcpStream::connect has already forgotten the hostname by the time Host: must be sent; the rule states both as one falsifiable contract with a worked request-builder

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source demonstrates this with a live TCP connection to a real host; the rule's example builds the request string and asserts its headers rather than opening a socket, since the compile-check harness has no network access

entries.title: 10.2.4 Effect of spawning many threads

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("10.2.4 Effect of spawning many threads", p.359) demonstrates that a CPU-bound workload's throughput collapses past physical-core thread count, and that thread::sleep is a request to the scheduler rather than a deadline; the rule states both as a falsifiable contract plus the yield_now-vs-spin_loop distinction the source covers in the surrounding pages

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's demonstration is a benchmark run on the author's machine; the rule's assertion proves the pool-sizing function and the sleep-then-spin pause never returns early, not the throughput-collapse curve itself, which needs a real multi-core benchmark to observe

entries.title: 6.4.1 Background

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("6.4.1 Background", p.228) opens the virtual memory chapter this rule draws on: allocation success does not mean physical backing, and the first write to a page is where the real commit and OOM risk occur; the rule states the first-touch benchmarking discipline this observation implies

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source explains virtual memory as OS background for scanning a process's own address space, not specifically as a benchmarking pitfall; the first-touch-before-timing framing and its assertion are this rule's own addition

entries.title: Parsing Command-Line Arguments Using clap

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Parsing Command-Line Arguments Using clap", p.58) walks through get_matches, which prints usage and exits the process on a bad argv, and later pages in the same chapter show a value_name/id mismatch returning None at runtime; the rule states both as a deliberate contract choice (try_parse_from for a Result, keeping id and value_name conceptually separate) plus the ArgGroup::required, allow_hyphen_values, and declaration-order-positional gotchas the book's later chapters hit tool by tool

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source demonstrates get_matches-based parsing across many chapters without naming try_get_matches/try_parse as the alternative in this section specifically; the assertion proves the Result-returning path compiles and behaves as documented, not that every gotcha listed in the rule's Contract is individually demonstrated

entries.title: Preserving Line Endings While Reading a File

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Preserving Line Endings While Reading a File", p.149) states exactly this rule's contract: BufRead::lines() strips terminators and fabricates a rewritten ending, so a byte-faithful tool must read_line into a reused buffer and print without adding a newline; the rule restates it as a general contract with CRLF and missing-final-newline fixtures

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source demonstrates this with read_line specifically; the rule's assertion additionally covers read_until and a CRLF fixture, which the cited page does not itself include a worked example for

entries.title: Adding state

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Adding state", p.71) demonstrates values built inside the per-worker application factory being invisible across workers (server_id/request_count desync across curls); the rule states the general fix (build shared state outside the factory, clone a handle in) and extends it to the typed-extension-map half of request-scoped state the unit does not cover

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's worked example is Actix-specific; the rule's typed-extension-map contract is a generalization to the same pattern in Axum/Rocket/Tower that the source does not itself demonstrate

entries.title: Writing a custom derive

exact_difference.detail: the unit ("Writing a custom derive", p.281) builds a derive macro and, in the surrounding pages, introduces helper attributes and the fact that a proc macro sees only tokens before type checking; the rule states the general contract (declare via attributes(...), cannot query trait impls, parse with syn::parse::Parse, skip attributes the macro does not own) as a falsifiable pattern

entries.remaining_uncertainty: the source's helper-attribute parsing is demonstrated across several pages of one worked derive; the rule's example is a condensed, independently-verified restatement rather than the book's own code
